newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: INTERVIEW - Emerging markets bank Caspian eyes Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Emerging markets bank Caspian eyes Asia.

text.p: Start-up investment bank Caspian Holdings SCA is expanding fast in Asia as part of its plans to focus on emerging markets, a senior company official said.
After establishing itself in Latin America, the company is targeting the Asian market next, Caspian Research (Malaysia) Sdn Bhd managing director, Steve Clayton said in an interview.
Offices in eastern Europe will follow.
Caspian, started by former Barings chief executive Christopher Heath in late 1995, now has research offices in Mexico, Argentina and Brazil.
It has also opened offices in Hong Kong, Bombay, New Delhi, Kuala Lumpur and Bangkok.
Offices in Taipei, Manila and Jakarta are also being considered, Clayton said.
He said unlike the larger research houses which cover both developed and developing markets, Caspian will focus on the emerging markets of Latin America, Asia and eastern Europe.
"We are 100 percent committed to emerging markets. We are not interested in developed markets in the West like the U.S., U.K. markets," Clayton said. "We are focusing on high growth markets."
Recent industry consolidation which saw big investment banks gobbling up smaller competitors cut the number of so-called boutique houses, and provided Caspian with its window of opportunity, he said.
"The niche is being created as a result of all previous niche players in emerging markets being acquired by the larger investment banks," Clayton said.

He pointed to the acquisition of British houses Barings, Smith New Court and Kleinwort Benson by Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV, Merrill Lynch of the U.S. and Germany's Dresdner Bank AG, respectively, as some examples.
"Those companies became part of bigger groups which are part of developed markets," he said.
Caspian Holdings earlier this month announced it has raised $85 million via a rights issue to existing shareholders to expand the company's capital to $100 million.

The new money, which included cash from investors in Korea, Thailand, Singapore, India and Mexico, would enable Caspian to expand into corporate finance and asset management, Caspian chief executive Heath said. The company has opened 150 institutional accounts.
Caspian currently has around 170 staff worldwide and will have up to 500 eventually, Clayton said.
In Asia, the company plans to have about 100 staff, with a third based in Hong Kong, its regional sales and dealing centre.
Its Kuala Lumpur office is the only Asian office so far with a full headcount of seven research analysts. The other offices are being built-up gradually, Clayton said.
